method: Static only: atomscan slow scans and cleave facts for all samples and archive binaries; resolved dnfile/dncil IL for installer and embedded application; Rizin/Capstone native route registration, middleware and handler dispatch; recovered repository/dependency sources and publisher binary. No specimen executed.

evidence: Tarball contains only package.json and a stripped Rust ELF. Manifest has no install scripts or runtime package dependencies. Current upstream repository version 0.1.1 matches API strings, routes, data types and native control flow; this is correspondence, not a reproducible binary build.

Main loads CAP_TESTER_PORT at 0x2589c9 and HOST at 0x258b4b. The router registers /api/fs/read at 0x2599c3 and /api/fs/write at 0x259aa1. Read handler wrapper 0x2c731c installs vtable 0x7ea108, whose call target 0x2bffad constructs the request future with poll target 0x28de1c. Write wrapper 0x2c73cc uses its distinct vtable/dispatch 0x2c01db. Source binds caller-supplied paths to std::fs read/write and directory enumeration.

Auth middleware at 0x2a5cd6 compares authorization with configured credentials, branches to the Basic challenge at 0x2a5d31 when unequal, and forwards authorized requests at 0x2a5d78. Source defaults to 127.0.0.1:4173, with explicit host/port/auth overrides. TCP/UDP listener, echo/send and Zenoh pub/sub routes require requests; no fixed external collection destination or command-execution route was found.

agealt-svc is concatenated HTTP vocabulary, not a daemon helper. application/x-httpd-php is a MIME entry, not an Apache process. Base64/hex/XOR decoder candidates are fragments of constants and parser diagnostics; no staged executable or concealed endpoint is established.
samples.source_label_explanation: Exact Aikido rationale unavailable. New platform packages exposing broad local file/socket APIs and large TLS-enabled native binaries could explain a heuristic listing; no malicious payload was found. Deployment authorization and actual use are unknown.

evidence: Tarball contains only the platform manifest and stripped Rust Mach-O. It implements the same local browser/native capability service as the ELF.

AArch64 main loads port/host configuration at 0x1000312ec/0x10003142c, defaults port to 0x104d (4173) at 0x100031364, and copies 127.0.0.1 at 0x100031480. Router construction registers fs/read at 0x100031fe8 and fs/write at 0x100032088. Middleware compares credential bytes at 0x100070670, forwards equality at 0x100070704, and constructs Basic realm challenge on failure at 0x1000706cc.

Invalid user-password dictionary file belongs to Zenoh transport authentication, not online password guessing. Fetched zenoh-config 1.10.1 declares transport.auth.usrpwd.dictionary_file, TLS connect/listen_private_key fields, and gateway configuration. Their concatenated serialization field names explain the gateway private-key false match. Rustls/AES/ChaCha code supports transport security; no credential-exfiltration path was found.
samples.source_label_explanation: Exact Aikido rationale unavailable; same native-capability and new-package concerns as Linux. No covert payload or fixed hostile endpoint was found; non-loopback deployment without auth would expose powerful dual-use APIs.

evidence: Unsigned IL-only .NET GUI installer, managed entry token 0x06000007, IeoPreviewInstaller.Main at RVA 0x2b44. Version fields are blank/0.0.0.0; manifest requests asInvoker. Publisher website links this exact SHA256-named download, fetched with forager hash verification; bytes equal the submitted file.

Installer confirms with the user, confines installation to LocalApplicationData/Programs, validates archive hash and every member size/SHA256, prevents absolute/traversing paths and duplicate ZIP entries, stages releases then atomically moves them, and creates owned desktop/Start-menu shortcuts and HKCU uninstall registration. All 226 ZIP members match the embedded manifest. Uninstall removes owned shortcuts/startup value while preserving library and versions.

Run-key setter in installer is guarded by an existing command belonging to this install and ending in the known --hidden suffix; it preserves opt-in startup on update rather than silently enabling it. Process lookup checks its own application and asks the user to exit. COM/dynamic calls create shortcuts, not downloaded-code dispatch. Installer performs no remote fetch or shell launch.

Embedded ieo-native.exe resolved IL implements a WebView2 PDF reader, local reading history/migration and Google Drive sync. Native web messages and navigation are restricted to the exact internal ieo.example origin. OAuth uses external browser consent, loopback redirect, state and PKCE S256; refresh tokens use CurrentUser DPAPI. Startup registration is exposed through the application setting. JavaScript uploads app reading records to the user's Google Drive appDataFolder and reads explicitly selected PDFs, with no unrelated collection sink found.

Bundled WebView2 Core/WinForms/Loader Authenticode signatures verify OK in LIEF and identify Microsoft Corporation. ZIP assets include PDF.js codecs/workers/sample PDFs. The original PE scan does not recursively expose managed ZIP resources, so those bytes were extracted and independently analyzed; no suspended-process injection, obfuscating loader or secret theft was found.
samples.source_label_explanation: Unsigned preview packaging, blank version fields, a large compressed managed resource, reflection/COM, self-copy and registry startup support plausibly trigger generic ML engines. Exact collection circumstances and user authorization are unavailable; publisher-byte identity and reviewed behavior support likely benign, not proof of every deployment.

rule_changes.change: Move password-dictionary-input to os/security/auth/password::password-dictionary-file-reference with identical matcher/scope/criticality; update cracking consumer.
rule_changes.reason: A dictionary-file error is ordinary authentication configuration, not evidence of guessing. No matching content removed. Two broad credential-access consumers are JavaScript-only and cannot select the Mach-O-scoped atom.

rule_changes.change: Move/rename daemon helper name token to process/info/name and exclude exact agealt-svc.
rule_changes.reason: Matcher proves one name token, not command-line access or a cluster. Observed match is concatenated HTTP headers. The sole exact masquerade consumer follows the move; positive helper/masquerade controls pass.

rule_changes.change: Require non-hyphen boundaries around httpd/apache2 service names. Retain the canonical httpd-name atom and rename the formerly overlapping combined atom to apache2-name-reference; update its native-web-service-names consumer.
rule_changes.reason: application/x-httpd-php is a content type, not a service name. Preserve standalone executable names, executable paths and apache2.service. The old Apache atom duplicated the HTTPD observation; its consumer now uses the existing canonical HTTPD atom plus the distinct Apache2 atom.

rule_changes.change: Require a leading key-name boundary in gateway public/private-key proximity patterns.
rule_changes.reason: Zenoh connect_private_key...gateway is TLS configuration; Braintree PrivateKey/PublicKey diagnostics remain matched. Existing malicious NuGet fixture and all five DLL variants retain every original finding, including gateway theft.

rule_changes.change: Add generic Basic realm challenge reference under HTTP auth.
rule_changes.reason: Native credential-check branches implement this protocol. Raw matcher for ELF/Mach-O/PE recovers bytes split into Basic/realm tokens by text extraction; the native-only scope satisfies the raw-matcher type cap.

rule_changes.change: Move existing ConPTY/conhost co-reference from process/info/name to process/tty/pty, with identical scope/matcher/severity.
rule_changes.reason: PTY context is more specific than a generic process name. This also keeps the process-name leaf at its existing 100-rule budget. No exact or directory-selector consumers select the old rule; positive/near-miss controls cover the move.

verification.focused_controls: 8 cases: HTTP vocabulary, standalone daemon names, helper masquerade, ordinary Zenoh auth/TLS, cracking composite, ConPTY near miss/positive, and existing Braintree malware archive.
verification.braintree_full_comparison: No added or lost findings across archive and all five embedded framework DLLs.
verification.material_detection_losses: Only unsupported MIME/header daemon and concatenated TLS-key claims removed. Dictionary reference retained at notable in neutral home. No supported hostile coverage lost.
verification.disagreements: All batch files and archive members remain without suspicious/hostile findings. Calibrated ML routes remain benign; PE raw probability remains 0.6752126. External malicious source labels disagree with these likely-benign judgments; collection/deployment context is unavailable.
verification.validator_setup: Installed atomscan-linked validator has an older 100-rule naming budget. Baselines/final comparisons used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 without changing rules. Checkout-built /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/target/release/cleave recognizes the reviewed naming=101 budget; final make validate uses that engine explicitly.
verification.final_rerun: Final atomscan scans after validation-driven corrections retain the recorded sample/child findings and probabilities. No suspicious or hostile rule fires in the batch.
